insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for modeled attribution. This protocol settles verified purchase confirmation at ~$0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost difference rooted in eliminating the attribution problem entirely, not solving it more efficiently.

With Chrome deprecating cookies and device fingerprinting increasingly blocked, the industry's primary cross-site tracking primitives are gone. Cryptographically verified, identity-free receipts are structurally different from every probabilistic replacement currently on the market.

insights.topic: Closed-loop data is the wrong benchmark
insights.insight: Fetch and Ibotta hold verified receipt data, but it is identity-attached and not queryable by third parties. The relevant comparison is not whether verified receipt data exists — it does — but whether it is accessible without creating a privacy liability. This protocol is the only system that is simultaneously verified, identity-free, and publicly queryable.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases. Walmart knows Walmart purchases. Neither has cross-ecosystem visibility. Any aggregate commerce signal that resolves across retailer boundaries without individual identity exposure represents an information advantage no single first-party data stack can replicate.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion follows social graph, not media spend
insights.insight: Ten new metros activated in a single cycle — coast-to-coast, with non-metro California and Arkansas entering simultaneously despite no geographic adjacency. The burst-silence-burst pattern is word-of-mouth propagation with latency, not a paid funnel. Organic reach into non-metro markets is already established.

insights.topic: Unknown merchant category as data quality signal
insights.insight: 11% of receipts resist standard merchant classification, carrying a $290 average basket versus $52 for grocery — 5.5x higher. This likely reflects high-ticket or B2B transactions. Metrics dependent on merchant resolution, including category entropy and cross-domain balance, carry that 11% uncertainty and should be read as interpreted, not verified.
